I have 8 mu of land. Six mu I use for wheat and then maize, back to back, that is my main field. Two mu I plant cotton because the price was alright last year and I need cash for my family. I never went to school, so I do what my mother taught me and what I see the good farmers in the east of the village doing. If they use something and their field looks green and heavy, I use it too.

For wheat, I plant the improved variety I buy from the seed shop in town, the same one as last year. Before sowing I put one 50-kilo bag of compound fertilizer on each mu, the kind with three numbers on the bag. Then at green-up I spread half a 50-kilo bag of urea on each mu. Last year this gave me about 550 kilos per mu, which is enough to feed my family and sell a little. I run the rotary tiller before sowing to break up the maize stubble. I irrigate three times: once in winter if the ground is too dry, once at jointing, and once when the heads are filling. I spray twice, once for weeds after sowing and once in spring if I see aphids. I will do the exact same this year. I would rather put a little too much fertilizer than risk a thin crop. A bad wheat year means we eat less, and that is worse than wasting some money on an extra half bag.

For summer maize, I plant hybrid seed right after the wheat comes off the field in June. I use the same fertilizer as wheat: one bag of compound per mu at sowing, and half a bag of urea later when the plants are knee-high. Maize grows fast and needs water when it tassels, so I irrigate twice if the summer rains do not come. Two sprays: herbicide at the start, and one for armyworm if I see holes in the leaves. I rotary till quick after wheat harvest so I can get the seed in fast before the soil dries. I expect around 650 kilos per mu. Last year I got about that much.

For cotton on my two mu, I plough deep in spring because cotton roots go deep and the soil gets hard. I plant the improved cotton seed in April. I put one bag of compound per mu and half a bag of urea, same as my other crops. Some dealer once told me cotton needs different food, but I have always done it this way and it works on my field. Cotton needs more spraying because the bollworms are bad around here — I will spray four times, more if I see worms. I irrigate three times, at flowering and when the bolls are getting fat. I expect about 280 kilos of seed cotton per mu. My neighbor Lao Wang got nearly 300 last year with the same seed, so I hope I can too.

Everything costs money now. A bag of compound is more than 100 yuan, and urea is not cheap either. But my husband works off-farm and my eldest son sends some money back, so I can buy the inputs. I do not dare cut back. Two years ago I tried saving half a bag of urea on one mu of maize and the plants turned yellow and small. Never again. I watch my neighbors and copy what works.
